source_text: Περὶ διαφορᾶς εὐνούχων. «Εἰσὶ γὰρ εὐνοῦχοι οἵτινες ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς ἐγεννήθησαν οὕτως» ἕως τοῦ «Ὁ δυνάμενος χωρεῖν χωρείτω.» Δύο ἐσομένας περὶ τὸν τόπον τοῦτον παρεκδοχὰς πρὸ τῆς φαινομένης ἡμῖν ἀληθοῦς εἰς τὸν τόπον διηγήσεως ἐκθέμενοι, καὶ μετὰ τοῦτο ὡς δυνατὸν ἡμῖν ἀνατρέψαντες αὐτάς, ἵν’ ὅσον ἐπὶ τοῖς λεχθησομένοις πᾶν σφάλμα φυλαξάμενοι τὸ ἀληθὲς βούλημα χωρῶμεν, οὕτως ἥκωμεν ἐπὶ τὸ προκείμενον. Τινὲς μὲν γάρ, ὡς ἀκόλουθον τοῖς κατὰ τὸ σωματικὸν ὁρωμένοις δύο εὐνουχισμοῖς καὶ τὸν τρίτον σωματικὸν νομίσαντες, ἐτόλμησαν ἑαυτοὺς παρασχεῖν ὑπὸ φόβου μὲν τοῦ πρὸς Θεὸν ἀνεπιστημόνως δὲ εὐνουχισμῷ ὁμογενεῖ τοῖς δύο προτέροις, καὶ ἑαυτοὺς ὑποβεβλήκασιν ὀνειδισμῷ τάχα δὲ καὶ αἰσχύνῃ οὐ παρὰ μόνοις τοῖς ἀλλοτρίοις τῆς πίστεως. Ἕτεροι δὲ οὐ πολλοὶ τοὺς μὲν προτέρους δύο αὐτόθεν καὶ σωματικῶς ἐξειλήφασιν εἰρῆσθαι τῷ Σωτῆρι, τὸν δὲ τρίτον οὐκέτι κατὰ τὴν λέξιν ἀλλ’ εὐνουχισμὸν ἡγήσαντο τὸν ἀπὸ λόγου σημαίνεσθαι, ὅτε προθέσει τῆς τῶν οὐρανῶν βασιλείας τῷ τμητικωτάτῳ λόγῳ ἐκτεμόντες τὸ ἐπιθυμητικὸν καταπεφρονήκασι τῶν ὕβρεων τοῦ σώματος.
thought_title: Two misreadings of the three eunuchs
orientation: Origen begins his treatment of Matthew 19:12 by laying out two wrong interpretations of the three kinds of eunuchs before giving his own true reading.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning the difference of eunuchs. "For there are eunuchs who were born thus from their mother's womb" up to "Let the one who is able to receive it receive it." Having set out two misinterpretations that will arise about this passage before the true explanation of the passage that appears to us, and after this having refuted them as far as we are able, so that, as far as concerns what will be said, having guarded against every error we may receive the true meaning, thus let us come to the matter at hand. For some, having thought the third eunuchism also bodily as following the two eunuchisms seen according to the bodily sense, dared to offer themselves, out of fear of God but ignorantly, to a eunuchism of the same kind as the two former, and they subjected themselves to reproach and perhaps also to shame not only among those outside the faith. But others, not many, took the former two to have been said by the Savior immediately and bodily, but the third no longer according to the letter, but they considered a eunuchism from reason to be signified, when by purpose of the kingdom of the heavens, having cut out the desiring part with the most cutting reason, they have despised the outrages of the body.

choices.why: The noun denotes a wrong taking or reading alongside the true sense; 'misinterpretations' captures the interpretive error Origen will refute.
The verb means to overturn or demolish an argument; 'having refuted' fits Origen's polemical procedure against the two views.
The verb τολμάω carries the sense of bold or reckless daring, and παρασχεῖν ἑαυτούς means to hand themselves over; the rendering keeps the self-destructive agency.
rejected: had the audacity to present themselves

choices.why: The superlative adjective modifies λόγος as the rational principle that severs the passions; 'most cutting' preserves the surgical metaphor.
The substantivized adjective denotes the appetitive or desiring faculty of the soul in philosophical psychology; 'the desiring part' keeps the technical sense.

choices.english: they have despised the outrages of the body
choices.why: ὕβρεις here means the insolent assaults or abuses of the body against the soul; 'outrages' preserves the violent, insulting force.

bible_refs.note: εἰσὶ γὰρ εὐνοῦχοι οἵτινες ἐκ κοιλίας μητρὸς ἐγεννήθησαν οὕτως ... ὁ δυνάμενος χωρεῖν χωρείτω

pass_b_english: On the difference among eunuchs. “For there are eunuchs who were born that way from their mother’s womb,” up to “Let the one who is able to receive this receive it” (Matthew 19:12). Before giving the interpretation of this passage that appears true to us, I will set out two misinterpretations that are going to arise about this text, and then refute them as far as I am able, so that by guarding against every error in what will be said, we may grasp the true meaning and so come to the matter at hand.

Some people, thinking that the third kind of eunuch is bodily just as the two bodily eunuchisms they saw were, dared to offer themselves to a eunuchism of the same kind as the first two—out of fear of God, but without understanding—and they have subjected themselves to reproach and perhaps even to shame, and not only among those outside the faith alone.

Others, not many, have taken the first two kinds as spoken by the Savior in a straightforward bodily sense, but they have understood the third no longer according to the letter, but as the eunuchism that comes from reason, when by purpose for the kingdom of heaven they have cut out the desiring part with the most cutting reason and have despised the outrages of the body.

problems.quote: and not only among those outside the faith.
problems.source_quote: οὐ παρὰ μόνοις τοῖς ἀλλοτρίοις τῆς πίστεως
problems.why: Source says 'not only among those outside the faith' but English drops 'only' (μόνοις), weakening the claim.
problems.fix: and not only among those outside the faith alone.
problems.ruling: μόνοις ('only') is present in source but absent in English, changing 'not only' to 'not...only' misrepresents scope of reproach.

edits.old: and not only among those outside the faith.
edits.new: and not only among those outside the faith alone.

fixed: Added 'alone' to render μόνοις, which the English had dropped.

last_rejected.quote: out of fear of God, but without understanding
last_rejected.source_quote: ὑπὸ φόβου μὲν τοῦ πρὸς Θεὸν ἀνεπιστημόνως δὲ
last_rejected.why: ἀνεπιστημόνως modifies the eunuchism, not their understanding: 'unskillfully/inexpertly', not 'without understanding' as a separate clause about their mental state.
last_rejected.fix: out of fear toward God, yet unskillfully, to a eunuchism of the same kind as the first two
last_rejected.ruling: ἀνεπιστημόνως means 'without understanding/ignorantly'; adverb modifying the action; rendering is within normal range.

last_rejected.why: λόγος here is 'word' (Scripture/word of God), not human 'reason'; this is a technical term for the divine Word that cuts.
last_rejected.ruling: λόγος can mean 'reason'; τμητικός suggests cutting/reasoning; not clearly wrong within word's semantic range.

last_rejected.quote: have despised the outrages of the body
last_rejected.why: ὕβρεις means 'insults' or 'abuses' suffered from the body, not 'outrages' committed by it; the sense is contempt for the body's mistreatment/temptations.
last_rejected.fix: have despised the insults of the body
last_rejected.ruling: ὕβρεις can mean 'outrages'; 'outrages of the body' captures contempt for bodily excesses; within normal range.
